claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy is a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution.
The initial alloy has a continuous passive oxide layer.
Thermal exposure under service conditions causes slow nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Mg-rich intermetallic compounds form primarily at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
The intermetallic compounds sequester corrosion- and oxidation-protective elements from the matrix.
Sequestration of protective elements changes the composition of the surface oxide.
The altered surface oxide lowers high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the initial state.
Intermetallic formation and the resulting oxide alteration lower corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
Rapid quenching suppresses intermetallic nucleation and maintains a stabilized comparison state.
Thermally activated diffusion promotes segregation of Mg and co-alloying elements into intermetallic phases.
The intermetallic transformation follows sigmoidal kinetics.
The transformation has a threshold temperature of approximately 600°C.
Intermetallic nucleation becomes significant near or above approximately 600°C after prolonged exposures such as more than 50 hours.
Matrix depletion associated with intermetallic formation makes the protective oxide layer chemically heterogeneous and less effective.
Aged samples will contain clearly identifiable Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
Aged samples will form non-protective mixed oxide scales.
Aged samples will have poorer high-temperature oxidation behavior and lower corrosion resistance than quench-stabilized controls.
The initial metastable single-phase solid solution has higher corrosion and oxidation resistance than the aged state.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says intermetallics deplete corrosion-/oxidation-protective elements, whereas the mechanism calls the depleted species corrosion-/oxidation-promoting elements. Read literally, depletion of elements that promote corrosion or oxidation would be expected to improve rather than degrade resistance.
